thread:
mia_cs: Heads-up: Northbridge onboarding failing during headless ramp. CI spins 180 browsers; ~20-30% preflights return 429 and a couple of 401s. Need quick unblock for renewal next week.

northbridge_se: Reproducer: each worker calls /session/new then immediately hits /v1/preflight. No shared cache across workers. Sample responses: "HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 1\nX-Request-Id: nb-77b" and "HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\nX-Request-Id: nb-77c"

arjun_sdk: Which SDK/version? Any custom session logic?

northbridge_se: node-browser-sdk@0.19.1, default session flow. Tests isolated so no cross-worker token reuse.

peng_eng: Sounds like token creation + immediate preflight is hitting preflight origin rate limits. Short-term: 1) add a tiny in-process token lease (2-4s TTL) so concurrent workers reuse one ephemeral token; 2) add randomized start jitter (0-300ms) across workers.

arjun_sdk: Example tiny snippet we recommend (Node runner): ```js// in-memory leaselet lease=null;async function getEphemeral(){ if(lease && Date.now()<lease.exp) return lease.t; const t=await fetch('/session/new').then(r=>r.text()); lease={t,exp:Date.now()+3000}; return t;}```

mia_cs: I'll request a temporary quota bump from RevOps while they run the patched test.

northbridge_se: Quick try: added 3s lease + 0-250ms jitter. Re-ran 180 parallel: 429s down to ~7%, 401s gone. Much better.

deploy-bot: NOTICE: rate-limit config rolled to preflight-service at 2026-03-19T17:30Z (rule: preflight-origin-3s).

arjun_sdk: That deploy likely tightened burst windows. For longer-term, SDK should expose an "ephemeralLease" option that coalesces session fetches per origin. We'll file a small RFC.

peng_eng: Also add NTP/time-sync check to onboarding checklist: we saw a 401 once when CI box clock was ~8s ahead. Ephemeral tokens are time-sensitive.

northbridge_se: Confirmed clock skew was the one 401; NTP sync removed it.

mia_cs: I'll capture these steps in a short runbook for Northbridge and keep the quota ticket open until full warmup completes.

arjun_sdk: If customers need higher concurrency warmups, recommend server-side warmup (one server actor doing sequential preflights) rather than many isolated browsers.

peng_eng: Engineering follow-up: consider soft buffering in preflight-service (200-500ms) to smooth cold-start spikes. Filing infra ticket.

northbridge_se: Thanks team — will run full suite overnight and report. Appreciate the quick responses.

mia_cs: Thanks everyone, tagging RevOps and product for awareness. :white_check_mark:
